title: Algerian semolina bread
subtitle: khobz el dar: fine semolina home bread with olive oil and sesame
excerpt: Khobz el dar is the everyday home bread of Algeria, made with fine semolina or a blend of semolina and plain flour, olive oil, and fast-action yeast. It bakes into a round, slightly domed loaf with a golden crust and a slightly denser, golden crumb than an all-flour loaf. Sesame or nigella seeds are scattered on top before baking. It is the bread most Algerian families make daily, eaten with harissa, olive oil, and the main meal.
sourceNotes: Semolina bread is the everyday household bread of Algeria and much of North Africa, where it is known variously as khobz, kesra, or matlou depending on thickness and shape. The use of fine durum wheat semolina (rather than the coarser semolina used in pasta) gives the bread its characteristic yellow crumb and slightly nutty flavour. The recipe is documented in North African culinary references including Samira Mahjoub's cookery books and community food collections.

glossaryTerms.definition: Ground durum wheat milled finer than the coarse semolina used in pasta. In bread baking it produces a denser crumb than plain flour, with a slightly nutty flavour and a golden colour from the high carotenoid content of durum wheat. It absorbs water more slowly than plain flour, so doughs made with semolina need a longer mixing time to fully hydrate.

content.text: Algerian semolina bread is a quick, simple loaf with no specialist shaping. Form the dough into a flat round, prove for 40 minutes, and bake.

Combine {{fine-semolina}}, {{plain-flour}}, {{yeast-fast-action}}, {{sea-salt-fine}}, and {{caster-sugar}} in a large bowl. Add {{water}} and {{olive-oil}} and mix to a rough dough. Leave to rest, uncovered, for 10 minutes to allow the semolina to absorb the water fully.

Knead for 10 minutes until the dough is smooth and slightly tacky. It will never be as smooth as a pure wheat flour dough; a little roughness is normal. Place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover, and leave at room temperature for 1 hour until noticeably puffed (it may not fully double in size; this is fine).

Turn the dough out and shape into a flat round about 22 cm in diameter. Place on a lined baking tray, cover loosely with oiled cling film, and prove for 40 minutes until puffed. Scatter {{sesame-seeds}} over the surface and press lightly to adhere. Dimple the surface all over with your fingertips.

Heat the oven to 200°C (conventional). Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden on top and the underside sounds hollow when tapped. The sesame seeds should be toasted and golden, not pale. Cool on a wire rack and eat the same day.
